post.topic: API privacy and hidden telemetry in developer tools
post.linkedin_text:
Are your API tools secretly sharing your data? Recent discoveries around unexpected auto-installed plugins in tools like Postman are a wake-up call for developers.

We install utilities for convenience. But convenience often comes with background data sharing we never agreed to.

Here is how to protect your workspace:

→ Audit your installed plugins and extensions monthly.
→ Monitor outbound network traffic from your development environment.
→ Read the changelogs before updating mission-critical tools.
→ Use local-first or open-source alternatives when handling sensitive client data.

Your API payloads belong to you and your clients. Don't let silent background defaults compromise your security.

What steps do you take to secure your local development stack?

slides.title: Is Your *API Tool* Secretly Sharing Your Data?
slides.body: Why silent telemetry in development software is a major risk.

slides.title: The Hidden Risk
slides.body: Many utilities auto-install AI features and plugins that may sync local API payloads to remote cloud servers without clear consent.

slides.title: Audit Your Extensions
slides.body: Regularly review installed plugins in your IDE and API clients. Remove anything you do not explicitly use or trust.

slides.title: Monitor Network Traffic
slides.body: Use tools like Wireshark or built-in proxy inspectors to check if your development environment is making unexpected outbound requests.

slides.title: Choose Local First
slides.body: When working with sensitive client endpoints, prioritize open-source and local-first tools that respect your workspace privacy.
